findings.problem: LeaseWorkflow exposes all fields as pub primitives (String, bool, Option<u64>). Status and sent flags are stored redundantly as separate fields, allowing inconsistent states such as status="sent" with is_sent=false, or status="draft" with is_sent=true. These are illegal states the compiler cannot prevent.
findings.failure_mode: A caller can set item.status = "sent" while leaving is_sent=false, or vice versa, producing a lease that is internally contradictory. Any downstream code reading status and is_sent independently may observe divergent facts about lease lifecycle.
findings.fix: Replace status, is_validated, and is_sent with a single typed state enum or typestate pattern (e.g. enum LeaseState { Draft, Validated, Sent { sent_at: Timestamp } }). Remove all pub bool/String lifecycle fields. Make the struct non-pub or use private fields with constructors.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool is a primitive lifecycle flag. Per the functional-core-performance reference, bool lifecycle flags must be replaced with enums or typestates to make the valid transition graph known to the compiler.
findings.failure_mode: Code can call mark_sent on a lease where is_validated=false, skipping validation entirely. No compile-time or runtime guard enforces the validated-before-sent invariant.
findings.fix: Represent validation as part of a typed state enum. Marking sent should require a LeaseState::Validated variant and return a typed error or a new state value; it cannot be called on Draft.

findings.problem: is_sent: bool is a primitive lifecycle flag that duplicates information already in status. Redundant bool/string lifecycle data is explicitly called out as unrepresentable of the domain invariants.
findings.failure_mode: is_sent can diverge from status, making the struct internally inconsistent. Consumers must check both fields and reconcile them, increasing bug surface.
findings.fix: Remove is_sent entirely. Encode 'sent' as a variant of the state enum carrying any needed metadata (e.g. sent_at). If sent_at is needed, store it inside the Sent variant, not as a separate Option<u64>.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no domain semantics. Lease identifiers have format rules, uniqueness invariants, and parsing requirements that a String cannot encode.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can pass an empty string, malformed ID, or duplicate ID into the workflow. Domain invariants about ID validity are not enforced at the type level.
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype LeaseId(String) or LeaseId(OwnedString) with a fallible constructor that validates format. Use LeaseId instead of String in the struct.

findings.problem: status: String allows arbitrary string values ("sent", "SENT", "", "pended", etc.) that have no domain meaning. This is primitive obsession in the core data type.
findings.failure_match: Match statements or string comparisons on status are brittle and incomplete. New invalid states can always be introduced by assigning an unexpected string.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with an enum LeaseStatus { Draft, Validated, Sent }. Remove the redundant is_sent field entirely.

findings.problem: mark_sent mutates the struct in place and does not validate any preconditions (is_validated must be true, status must not already be "sent"). It is a pure function in name but performs no domain validation.
findings.failure_mode: mark_sent can transition a non-validated lease to sent, violating the business invariant. Returns the mutated struct without any error signal.
findings.fix: Change mark_sent to accept a typed state value (e.g. LeaseState) and return Result<LeaseWorkflow, LeaseError::AlreadySent | LeaseError::NotValidated>. Validate preconditions before transitioning.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> stores epoch milliseconds as a raw u64 with no domain semantics. When sent, this should be enforced by the type system (present exactly when state is Sent).
findings.failure_mode: sent_at_epoch_ms can be Some with a stale/out-of-range epoch, or None when status="sent". The coupling between state and timestamp is not enforced.
findings.fix: Tuck sent_at inside the Sent state variant (e.g. LeaseState::Sent { sent_at: Instant }). Use a proper timestamp type. Remove the standalone Option<u64> field.

findings.problem: All struct fields are pub. Consumers can mutate fields directly without any domain logic or validation, bypassing the functional core entirely.
findings.failure_mode: Any crate caller can do item.status = "invalid_value"; item.is_validated = false; and corrupt the lease state without any check.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide constructors (e.g. LeaseWorkflow::draft(id)) and state-transition methods that return Result or new state values. Expose only read-only accessors where needed.

findings.problem: mark_sent returns LeaseWorkflow directly with no error type. State transition failures must be communicated via typed domain errors, not by silently producing invalid state.
findings.failure_mode: Callers have no way to distinguish a successful sent transition from a no-op or silent failure. Errors are lost.
findings.fix: Define a domain error enum: pub enum LeaseError { AlreadySent, NotValidated }. Have mark_sent return Result<LeaseWorkflow, LeaseError>.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for any stated performance claim
no profiler output or allocation analysis for mark_sent or LeaseWorkflow lifecycle
no command evidence (cargo fmt, cargo test, cargo clippy) was run or reported
no try_reserve or bounded allocation handling (low-risk for this struct but absent)
no checked arithmetic anywhere in the crate (low-risk given no arithmetic present)
residual_risk: Static review only with no commands run. The crate has no compilation evidence, no tests, no benchmarks, and no formal verification. The dominant risk is illegal state representation: the struct can encode any combination of status/validated/sent values, making the core domain model fundamentally untrustworthy. Fix must be structural (typestates replacing bool/string primitives) before any incremental improvements are meaningful.
